items.title: The real dominated-extension principle as an additional hypothesis over ZF
items.statement: HB means: for every real vector space X, real-valued sublinear p:X→R, real linear subspace M≤X, and real linear g:M→R with g(m)≤p(m), there exists real linear F:X→R with F|M=g and F(x)≤p(x) for every x. This is an additional principle over ZF, not an assertion that ZF proves it.
items.strategy: Define the named assertion with all quantifiers. No Zorn theorem, choice ledger, BPI implication, or metamathematical non-implication is invoked. Norms and complex spaces enter only in later consequences.
items.axiom_strength: ZF defines the assertion HB; HB is not proved here

items.title: Dominated extension conditional on the relative principle
items.statement: Assume HB. Given X,M,p,g as in the principle, a real linear extension F exists on all X with -p(-x)≤F(x)≤p(x). No topology, closedness, or completeness is required.
items.strategy: Instantiate the quantified principle with the named data; apply F(-x)≤p(-x) and linearity for the lower bound. This is a conditional theorem, not the published Zorn implementation.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + the explicitly assumed relative Hahn–Banach principle

items.title: Relative norm-preserving Hahn–Banach extension over the real and complex fields
items.statement: Assume HB. For a normed space X over K=R or C, any K-linear subspace M, and bounded K-linear g:M→K, there is F∈X* with F|M=g and ||F||=||g||. M need not be closed and X need not be complete; M={0} is allowed.
items.strategy: Real case: p(x)=||g||||x|| is sublinear; the two signed bounds give |F(x)|≤p(x), while restriction gives the reverse norm inequality. Complex case: extend Re g as a real functional U with U≤||g||||·||, then put F(x)=U(x)-iU(ix). For F(x)≠0 use the explicit phase a=conj(F(x))/|F(x)| to get |F(x)|=U(ax)≤||g||||x||; treat F(x)=0 separately. Check extension by the real-part lemma. No family of phase choices or Zorn application.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + the explicitly assumed relative Hahn–Banach principle

items.title: Relative dual norming, point separation, and recovery of the norm
items.statement: Assume HB. For each nonzero x∈X there is f∈X* with f(x)=||x|| (a nonnegative real, also over C) and ||f||=1. Thus X* separates distinct points and ||x||=max_{||f||≤1}|f(x)| for every x, including x=0 and the zero space. More generally, any family H⊆X* whose linear span is norm dense detects zero: if h(x)=0 for all h∈H, then x=0.
items.strategy: On Kx define g(ax)=a||x||. Nonzero x gives uniqueness of a and ||g||=1; apply relative extension. Apply this to x-y for separation. The universal upper estimate is the operator-norm bound; the lower estimate uses the one witness for the fixed x. At zero the zero functional attains the unit-ball maximum. Do not claim that every fixed functional attains its own norm or that a global simultaneous selection x↦f_x has been constructed. For the total-family version, fix f∈X* and ε>0, approximate f in operator norm within ε by a finite linear combination g of H, and bound |f(x)|=|(f-g)(x)|≤ε||x||. Thus all f vanish on x, giving x=0. This uses one approximation at a time, not a chosen sequence.

items.title: Evaluation defines a bounded scalar-linear map into the bidual
items.statement: For any real or complex normed X, X**=(X*)* and J_X(x)(f)=f(x) define a K-linear map J_X:X→X** with ||J_Xx||≤||x||. No injectivity is asserted without HB.
items.strategy: Use the operator-norm lemma to equip X* with its norm and hence define its dual using the already-published dual definition a second time. For fixed x, evaluation is K-linear in f and |f(x)|≤||f||||x||. Pointwise operations show K-linearity in x and the supremum gives contractivity. The definition of J_X is introduced by this construction and does not import the later duality page.
items.axiom_strength: ZF; no HB or choice needed

items.title: Relative Hahn–Banach makes the canonical bidual map an isometry
items.statement: Assume HB. The canonical scalar-linear map J_X:X→X** is an isometry: ||J_Xx||=||x|| for every x. It is injective; surjectivity is not claimed.
items.strategy: Combine the evaluation upper bound with a norm-one functional norming the fixed nonzero x. At x=0 equality is immediate. If J_Xx=J_Xy, isometry applied to x-y gives x=y.

items.title: Convex sets and continuous real-hyperplane separation in a normed space
items.statement: Convex means closed under (1-t)x+ty for real 0≤t≤1, also in a complex space viewed as real. A continuous real hyperplane is {x:Re f(x)=a} for a∈R and nonzero f∈X*. Weak separation means Re f(A)≤a≤Re f(B); open-side strict separation means Re f(x)<a≤Re f(y) for all x∈A,y∈B. Uniform strict separation means Re f(x)≤a-ε<a+ε≤Re f(y) for some ε>0. Over R, Re f=f.
items.strategy: Introduce the conventions without identifying pointwise strict inequalities with a uniform gap. From a bound for f, Re f is Lipschitz; the level set is closed by an epsilon-ball argument. A nonzero complex-linear f has nonzero real part (rotate one nonzero value). State explicitly that complex numbers themselves are never ordered.
items.axiom_strength: ZF definitions and elementary norm estimates

items.title: The finite gauge of an open convex neighbourhood of zero
items.statement: For an open convex U⊆X with 0∈U, define p_U(x)=inf{t>0:x/t∈U}. The infimum exists as a finite nonnegative real for each x. The scalar field for p_U is the underlying real field.
items.strategy: Choose one r>0 with B(0,r)⊆U. If t>||x||/r, then x/t∈U (and at x=0 every t>0 works), so the set is nonempty and bounded below by zero; invoke the earlier infimum property. This establishes the definition before using its algebraic properties. U need not be balanced or bounded. Inline examples: for an open unit ball the defining admissible scales give p(x)=||x||; in R² the strip U={(s,t):|s|<1} gives p_U(s,t)=|s| and is unbounded; the convex set {0} in a nonzero space is not absorbing and does not supply a finite gauge on all vectors. Check each directly from the admissible-scale set, so the examples do not assume symmetry for general U.
items.axiom_strength: ZF; no HB or choice needed

items.title: The open convex gauge is sublinear and recovers its set
items.statement: If B(0,r)⊆U as above, then 0≤p_U(x)≤||x||/r, p_U(tx)=t p_U(x) for real t≥0, p_U(x+y)≤p_U(x)+p_U(y), U={x:p_U(x)<1}, and |p_U(x)-p_U(y)|≤||x-y||/r. Symmetry is not asserted.
items.strategy: Positive homogeneity follows by changing the infimum variable, with t=0 separate. For s>p_U(x) and t>p_U(y), obtain admissible s′<s,t′<t using the infimum property; convexity with zero makes x/s and y/t members of U. A convex combination gives (x+y)/(s+t)∈U, then take arbitrarily close s,t. If p_U(x)<1, an admissible scale below 1 and convexity give x∈U. Conversely openness permits (1+δ)x∈U (x=0 separately), hence p_U(x)<1. The ball inclusion gives the upper bound by all t>||x||/r. Subadditivity in both directions gives the Lipschitz estimate. Never infer |F|≤p_U from F≤p_U.
items.axiom_strength: ZF; no HB or choice needed

items.title: Relative separation of an open convex set from an exterior point
items.statement: Assume HB. If C is a nonempty open convex subset of a real or complex normed X and z∉C, some nonzero f∈X* satisfies Re f(c)<Re f(z) for every c∈C.
items.strategy: Fix c0∈C, put U=C-c0 and v=z-c0. Then p_U(v)≥1 and v≠0. Define g(tv)=t for real t. For t≥0 domination follows from p_U(v)≥1; for t<0 it follows from p_U≥0. Extend g to a real F≤p_U using relative dominated extension. Applying the bound at ±x gives |F(x)|≤||x||/r. Since F(v)=1 and F(U)<1, translate back. In the complex case use f(x)=F(x)-iF(ix) and bound it by 2||x||/r or use the phase identity; Re f=F.
items.axiom_strength: ZF + the explicitly assumed relative Hahn–Banach principle

items.title: A compact set and a disjoint closed set have a positive norm-distance gap
items.statement: In a normed space X, if K is nonempty compact and C is nonempty closed with K∩C=∅, there exists δ>0 such that ||k-c||≥δ for every k∈K,c∈C. No convexity or completeness is needed.
items.strategy: Use the intrinsic open cover of K consisting of every K∩B(k,r) with k∈K, r>0, and B(k,3r)∩C=∅. This is a set of all admissible balls, not a family of radii chosen for every k. Closedness makes it a cover; the triangle inequality shows its members are open in K. Compactness yields a finite subcover. Obtain finitely many centre/radius witnesses, permissible in ZF by finite induction. Let δ be the minimum of their positive radii; if k lies in B(k_j,r_j), then ||c-k||≥||c-k_j||-||k-k_j||>2r_j≥δ. No minimizing sequence, sequential compactness, or countable choice.
items.axiom_strength: ZF; finite selections only, no countable choice

items.title: Relative geometric Hahn–Banach with the exact open, closed, and compact hypotheses
items.statement: Assume HB and let A,B be disjoint nonempty convex subsets of a real or complex normed X. (i) If A is open, there exist nonzero f∈X* and a∈R with Re f(x)<a≤Re f(y) for all x∈A,y∈B; if B is also open, the right inequality is strict too. Swap labels/sign if only B is open. (ii) If A is closed and B compact, there exist nonzero f∈X*, a∈R and ε>0 with Re f(x)≤a-ε<a+ε≤Re f(y) for all x∈A,y∈B. In particular a point outside a nonempty closed convex set is uniformly strictly separated from it.
items.strategy: (i) C=A-B is convex and open: for c=a-b use a ball around a, with b fixed. It excludes 0. Apply the previous point-separation lemma to (C,0); write u=Re f. All u(a)<u(b), so a0=sup u(A) exists using any b∈B as upper bound. For each a∈A perturb slightly in a fixed direction with u(v)>0 to show u(a)<a0. If B is open perturb in the negative direction to obtain a0<u(b). (ii) The gap lemma gives δ>0 between A and B. Thus A+B(0,δ/2) is open convex and disjoint from B. Apply (i). Put ρ=δ/2. The same f satisfies u(a)+ρ||u||≤a0≤u(b), because sup_{||h||<ρ}u(h)=ρ||u||. Establish that identity from the supremum definition, negation and scaling, using epsilon witnesses individually. Since u≠0, ||u||>0. Set ε=ρ||u||/2 and separator a=a0-ε. This proves a uniform gap without norm attainment, a nearest point, compactness-to-sequences, or a later geometric theorem. A singleton is compact directly: any intrinsic open cover has one member containing its sole point, which is a finite subcover. This verifies the final point-versus-closed-set specialization.

title: Norming and Separation under Hahn–Banach: Examples

items.title: An explicit norming functional for the finite-dimensional maximum norm
items.statement: For n≥1 and nonzero x∈K^n with ||x||∞=max_j|x_j|, let j be the least maximizing coordinate and set f_x(y)=conj(x_j)y_j/|x_j| (with real conjugation trivial). Then f_x(x)=||x||∞ and ||f_x||=1. At x=0 use f=0 for the unit-ball formula; in dimension zero there is no norm-one functional. At x=(1,1) in K², the two different coordinate functionals both norm x, displaying nonuniqueness.
items.strategy: Finite maxima exist and the least index is canonical. Check the norm axioms directly for the maximum norm, K-linearity, and |f_x(y)|=|y_j|≤||y||∞. Evaluate at y=(x_j/|x_j|)e_j to attain 1 on the unit ball. All displayed choices are explicit finite formulas, so the construction is in ZF and does not require HB. This illustrates the relative norming conclusion without invoking it. Check f1(y)=y1 and f2(y)=y2 each have norm one and value one at (1,1), but differ at (1,0).

items.title: Quantitative separation of a norm ball from an exterior point
items.statement: Assume HB. Let r≥0 and ||z-a||>r in a real or complex normed space. There is norm-one f with f(z-a)=||z-a||. Every x with ||x-a||≤r satisfies Re f(x)≤Re f(a)+r<Re f(z). The gap is ||z-a||-r>0; its midpoint defines a separator with margin (||z-a||-r)/2.
items.strategy: Norm z-a with the relative corollary. Apply Re f(x-a)≤|f(x-a)|≤||x-a|| and add Re f(a). The explicit midpoint yields the stated uniform margin, including r=0. For an open ball with r>0 the left estimate is strict. No best-approximation theorem or compactness of the ball is used.
